name: Question 1
problem:
$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{∗}^{a}{\int }_{b}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

The triple integral above is defined over the type III region given by

$$
S={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le x+1,\,-2\le y\le xz}.
$$

What is the value of $a+b?$
worked_solution:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,z)\le y\le {u}_{2}(x,z)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/0603bed12c6af74e46544d8bebc52362aed95a9a5ad7418ea4faaf228f3b5241.png)

 

If $R$ is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,z)=-2,\,{u}_{2}(x,z)=xz.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.
$$

 

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le x+1}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x+1}[{\int }_{-2}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dz\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x+1}{\int }_{-2}^{xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=(1)+(0)=1.
$$

∭Sf(x,y,z)dV=∫∗a∫b∗∫∗∗f(x,y,z)dydzdx The triple integral above is defined over the type III region given by S={(x,y,z):−1≤x≤1,0≤z≤x+1,−2≤y≤xz}. What is the value of a+b?

a
x+1
b
2
c
xz+1
d
2x
e
1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,u1(x,z)≤y≤u2(x,z)}.

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If R is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of f(x,y,z) over R as a mixed integral, as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dy]dA

In our case, we have

u1(x,z)=−2,u2(x,z)=xz.

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

∭Sf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫−2xzf(x,y,z)dy]dA.

Now, the region D is given by

D={(x,z):−1≤x≤1,0≤z≤x+1}.

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over D as a repeated integral, we get

∬D[∫0xzf(x,y,z)dy]dA=∫−11∫0x+1[∫−2xzf(x,y,z)dy]dzdx=∫−11∫0x+1∫−2xzf(x,y,z)dydzdx.

Finally,

a+b=(1)+(0)=1.
